Welcome to Dysart School
We are delighted to welcome you to Dysart School, a special academy dedicated to providing outstanding education and support for pupils with Severe Learning Difficulties and Complex Needs, including many with Autism. With 200 pupils across four sites in Tolworth, Surbiton, and North Kingston, we pride ourselves on creating a nurturing and caring environment where every individual is valued and supported to reach their full potential.
Safety and wellbeing are at the heart of Dysart School. Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to create a welcoming atmosphere where pupils feel secure and inspired to learn. We understand that emotional and mental health are vital to achievement, and our integrated approach supports pupils’ holistic development every day.
We warmly invite parents and carers to become part of the Dysart community. Whether you are exploring options for your child or seeking to understand more about our unique approach, we encourage you to sign up for one of our open mornings using the from on our website.
Together, we can create the rainbow of opportunities your child deserves.
Leigh Edser – Principal

Personalised Learning & Progress
At Dysart, we recognise that successful outcomes depend on more than academic achievement alone. Alongside subject knowledge and qualifications, every pupil develops the skills needed to communicate effectively, build positive relationships, manage their wellbeing, develop independence and participate meaningfully in their communities.
To support this, we have developed the Dysart Skill Ladders: a whole-school framework that maps the progression of learning and development across the essential skills that underpin lifelong success. These skill ladders provide a shared language for pupils, staff and families, helping us to identify, teach, celebrate and track progress in the areas that matter most for learning, independence and preparation for adulthood.
The Dysart Skill Ladders are embedded throughout the curriculum and are relevant to every pupil, regardless of age, pathway or accreditation route. They ensure that key skills are taught explicitly, practised regularly and applied across different contexts, enabling pupils to transfer their learning beyond the classroom.
Whether a pupil is following an Engagement Pathway, accessing the National Curriculum or working towards accreditation and qualifications, the Dysart Skills framework remains a consistent thread throughout their educational journey. Together, these skills provide the foundation for confidence, resilience, wellbeing, community participation and future success.
The Dysart Key Skills
The ability to understand, manage and reflect on emotions is essential for learning and wellbeing.
Pupils develop strategies to regulate their emotions, manage change, build resilience and participate successfully in learning and social situations.
Pupils are supported to become increasingly confident and effective learners.
This includes developing attention, memory, problem-solving, critical thinking, creativity and the ability to apply learning across different contexts.

Careers
Careers Across the Curriculum
At Dysart, careers education is not limited to a single lesson or key stage. It is embedded across the whole curriculum and begins from the earliest stages of a pupil’s education.
Across all key stages, pupils are supported to develop the skills, experiences and understanding they will need for adulthood. This includes communication, independence, decision-making, problem-solving, teamwork, self-advocacy and understanding the world around them.
As pupils progress through the school, careers learning becomes increasingly personalised and links closely to individual aspirations, EHCP outcomes, accreditation, work-related learning and preparation for adulthood. Pupils are given meaningful opportunities to explore different roles, workplaces and pathways, helping them understand their strengths, interests and possible next steps.
Our aim is for every pupil, whatever their starting point or level of need, to experience a curriculum that raises aspirations and prepares them for a fulfilling adult life.
Careers Programme
Please click on the tabs to find out more.
At Dysart School, we are committed to preparing every pupil for life beyond school by developing the confidence, independence and real-life skills they need for their future.
At Dysart, careers education is fully embedded across the curriculum and daily school life. Learning is purposeful, practical and rooted in real-life contexts, enabling pupils to develop and apply the skills they need for adulthood.
Pupils access a carefully sequenced range of opportunities, including:
These experiences are designed to build pupils’ independence, confidence and employability skills over time, ensuring they are well-prepared for their next stage.
Our careers programme is fully aligned with the Gatsby Benchmarks and rigorously evaluated using Compass+, ensuring it remains ambitious, inclusive and responsive to the needs of all our pupils.
Dysart has contributed to the national Careers Impact Review, advocating for developments to Compass+ to better reflect the needs of pupils with SEND and strengthen inclusive practice across the sector.
This ongoing evaluation enables us to identify strengths, drive continuous improvement and ensure our provision not only meets statutory requirements, but is meaningful, personalised and aspirational for every pupil.
Pupils’ individual careers journeys are carefully tracked over time, including their experiences, development of key skills, aspirations and destinations. As a result, pupils leave Dysart with increasing independence, confidence and the ability to make informed decisions, supporting successful transitions into their next stage of education, employment or adulthood.

How careers guidance is delivered
At Dysart School, careers education is embedded across the whole curriculum and begins from the earliest stages of a pupil’s journey. Pupils progressively develop the communication, confidence, independence, interests and life skills they need to prepare for adulthood and life beyond school.
From Key Stage 3 onwards, this becomes increasingly explicit through a structured, pathway-led careers programme. Pupils build on earlier learning through curriculum links, enterprise, work-related learning, employer encounters, community experiences and personalised transition planning, with opportunities becoming more focused and personalised as they move towards their next steps.
Aim:To introduce a structured Skills for Life pathway, enabling pupils to develop independence, communication and early work-related skills through purposeful, real-life experiences.
Aim:To develop pupils’ independence, confidence and employability skills through accredited learning and increasingly authentic experiences of work.
To prepare pupils for their next stage by developing independence, employability and life skills, enabling successful transition into education, employment or adult life.
Work towards accredited qualifications (e.g. Ascentis)
Accredited qualifications (e.g. Ascentis)
Vocational learning (e.g. hospitality, gardening, office skills)
Work experience and employability programmes
Independent living skills (e.g. travel, cooking, self-care)
Transition planning and next steps
We evaluate the impact of our careers programme through pupil progress, engagement in work-related learning, accreditation outcomes and successful transitions into further education, employment or supported pathways.
This is supported by pupil voice, destination data and ongoing review of individual outcomes.
Accreditations & Awards
At Dysart School, accreditation is carefully personalised to reflect each pupil’s strengths, needs and aspirations. Pupils work towards a range of Ascentis qualifications, alongside functional and personal progress pathways, ensuring their achievements are both meaningful and recognised.
Our offer is continually reviewed and adapted to remain ambitious, relevant and responsive. By combining internal recognition (Footprints awards) with externally accredited qualifications, we ensure all pupils experience success and are well-prepared for their next stage in education, employment or adulthood.

Orchard Hill College
Progression Within the Orchard Hill College Academy Trust Dysart is part of the Orchard Hill College Academy Trust, providing pupils with direct access to Orchard Hill College and its specialist post-16 pathways. This strong partnership ensures continuity of learning, enabling pupils to progress into further education with confidence, independence and the skills needed for adult life.
Richmond upon Thames College
Richmond upon Thames College is a further education college located in Twickenham that offers a broach and innovative curriculum for students age 16+/
Nescot College
Apprenticeships & Further Education Nescot offers a range of pathways including apprenticeships, vocational courses and supported learning programmes. Pupils can develop practical skills, gain qualifications and prepare for employment in a structured college environment.
St Piers School & College
Residential Living St Piers provides residential education for young people with SEND, supporting independence, life skills and preparation for adulthood within a structured and supportive living environment.
Great Oaks
Specialist / Sensory Great Oaks offers a personalised curriculum combining vocational, educational and sensory learning. Programmes are tailored to individual needs, supporting progression into adulthood and meaningful next steps.
Aurora Centre (Merton College)
Independent Living Skills The Aurora Centre offers specialist programmes focused on independence, communication and life skills, supporting pupils to build confidence and prepare for adult living.
Activate Learning (Merrist Wood College)
Vocational Skills Merrist Wood provides hands-on vocational courses, particularly in land-based studies such as horticulture, animal care and outdoor learning. These courses support pupils to develop practical work skills and independence.
Working in Partnership with Families
At Dysart, we believe strong relationships make the difference. By working closely with families, we create a supportive community where pupils feel understood, valued and able to grow in confidence and independence.

Guidance and Next Steps
We work closely with our pupils, families and a range of external agencies to ensure that each pupil’s personal development, further education and future pathways are carefully matched to their individual needs, while remaining aspirational and meaningful.
Guidance is provided at every key stage transition, supporting pupils and families to understand available options, including future destinations and the qualifications offered at Dysart.
We maintain strong links with further education providers to ensure that transitions beyond Dysart are well-planned, personalised and successful.
Dysart School is committed to providing high-quality careers guidance and advice. Our Provider Access Policy outlines how education and training providers can engage with pupils to share information about future opportunities.
We also work in partnership with a range of organisations to ensure our careers provision meets statutory requirements and reflects best practice. These include:
These partnerships help shape our careers programme and ensure pupils have access to meaningful, relevant and up-to-date opportunities beyond Dysart School.

This strong partnership ensures continuity of learning, enabling pupils to progress into further education with confidence, independence and the skills needed for adult life.
Richmond upon Thames College
Richmond upon Thames College is a further education college located in Twickenham that offers a broach and innovative curriculum for students age 16+/
Nescot College
Apprenticeships & Further Education Nescot offers a range of pathways including apprenticeships, vocational courses and supported learning programmes. Pupils can develop practical skills, gain qualifications and prepare for employment in a structured college environment.
St Piers School & College
Residential Living St Piers provides residential education for young people with SEND, supporting independence, life skills and preparation for adulthood within a structured and supportive living environment.
Great Oaks
Specialist / Sensory Great Oaks offers a personalised curriculum combining vocational, educational and sensory learning. Programmes are tailored to individual needs, supporting progression into adulthood and meaningful next steps.
Aurora Centre (Merton College)
Independent Living Skills The Aurora Centre offers specialist programmes focused on independence, communication and life skills, supporting pupils to build confidence and prepare for adult living.
Activate Learning (Merrist Wood College)
Vocational Skills Merrist Wood provides hands-on vocational courses, particularly in land-based studies such as horticulture, animal care and outdoor learning. These courses support pupils to develop practical work skills and independence.
Working in Partnership with Families
At Dysart, we believe strong relationships make the difference. By working closely with families, we create a supportive community where pupils feel understood, valued and able to grow in confidence and independence.

We work closely with our pupils, families and a range of external agencies to ensure that each pupil’s personal development, further education and future pathways are carefully matched to their individual needs, while remaining aspirational and meaningful.
Guidance is provided at every key stage transition, supporting pupils and families to understand available options, including future destinations and the qualifications offered at Dysart.

Accreditation – Ascentis Courses Offered
At Dysart, accreditation is personalised to each pupil’s pathway, strengths and starting point. We use Ascentis qualifications to recognise meaningful progress in communication, independence and preparation for adulthood.
Our Ascentis accreditation offer is continually reviewed to ensure it reflects the needs, strengths and aspirations of our pupils. We do not take a fixed approach; instead, we adapt our pathways and qualifications in response to pupils’ progress, emerging interests and Preparation for Adulthood outcomes.
We regularly review the impact of accreditation through pupil progress, engagement and real-life application, refining the offer to ensure it remains meaningful, ambitious and relevant. This ensures that accreditation at Dysart is not just about gaining a qualification, but about recognising what each pupil can do and preparing them for their next steps.

PE and Sport Premium
At Dysart School, physical development is a key part of our wider curriculum and preparation for adulthood offer. We use the Primary PE and Sport Premium to improve the quality, consistency and long-term impact of physical education, physical activity and wellbeing across the school. Our highly personalised and inclusive approach reflects the needs of our pupils and ensures all learners can access meaningful opportunities to develop confidence, communication, regulation, independence and participation.
Physical activity at Dysart is not viewed in isolation. It is closely linked to communication, emotional regulation, sensory processing, health, wellbeing and long-term quality of life outcomes. Through PE, swimming, enrichment and community participation, pupils are supported to engage successfully in meaningful physical experiences that strengthen both learning and preparation for adulthood.
Our PE curriculum is carefully adapted to meet the needs of our pupils. Communication-rich and regulation-supportive approaches enable all pupils to participate successfully, experience achievement and increasingly apply skills across school and community contexts.
Physical activity at Dysart supports pupils to:
Our staff use specialist SEND pedagogy and adaptive approaches to ensure physical activity is accessible and meaningful for all pupils. Communication, regulation and participation are prioritised throughout PE and physical development.
Physical development is closely linked to Dysart’s Capable Environments framework and preparation for adulthood approach, ensuring pupils feel safe, successful and ready to engage.

Swimming and Water Safety
Swimming is an important part of Dysart’s inclusive physical education and development offer. It supports water confidence, safety awareness, communication, sensory regulation and independence.
Pupils access personalised swimming offer adapted to their physical, sensory, communication and learning needs. Dysart has an on-site swimming pool, and secondary pupils attend a local leisure centre once a week, providing opportunities to practise their skills in a community setting.
Our swimming offer reflects Dysart’s values:
The national curriculum swimming and water safety outcomes are to:
We teach towards these outcomes through clear, achievable steps. Every pupil has opportunities to develop their skills, with teaching and support matched to their needs.
Some Dysart pupils achieve the national outcomes later in their education, towards the end of Key Stage 3, 4 or 5. Swimming and water safety teaching therefore continues beyond Year 6. Other pupils continue to work towards personalised outcomes with ongoing support.
Perform safe self-rescue in different water-based situations.
Recognising individual achievement
Alongside the national outcomes, we assess meaningful progress in water confidence, floating, movement, swimming strokes, safe entry and exit, signalling for help and responding to safety instructions.
We record whether pupils demonstrate skills independently, with prompts or with physical support. These individual achievements are recognised separately from meeting the full national outcomes.
Our aim is for every pupil to develop their swimming and water safety skills as far as possible, supporting greater independence, wellbeing and participation in leisure opportunities.

Leading with Integrity
Doing the right thing, in the right way, for the right reasons.
At OHCAT, governance is not just a statutory duty – it’s a vital part of how we lead with integrity, collaborate effectively, and make a meaningful impact. Our governors play a key role in ensuring our schools are safe, inclusive, and thriving environments for pupils and staff.
What Do Local Governors Do at Dysart School?
Local Governors form part of our Local Governing Body (LGB), a committee of the OHCAT Board. Our governors work collectively to:
Our Governance Principles
Our local Governors are guided by our four core principles:
Who Can Be a Governor on our Local Governing Body?
Our LGB constitution is:
Our governors come from diverse backgrounds and bring a range of skills. What unites them is a shared commitment to improving outcomes and transforming lives for all pupils.
How Governance Works
Our governors meet termly to review performance, discuss priorities, and make decisions. They also conduct school visits to gain first hand insight into our school’s day-to-day operations, monitor progress against improvement plans and see the impact of their work. Governors complete mandatory training each term and follow a code of conduct to ensure professionalism and accountability.
In addition, governors take on a link governor responsibility. There are 6 link roles required by Trustees:
These roles allow governors to focus on specific strategic priorities and contribute to deeper oversight and support.
Governors may also be asked to participate in additional duties, such as:
These responsibilities are vital to ensuring robust governance and reflect the Trust’s commitment to transparency, fairness, and continuous improvement.
“Governance helps us transform lives. By supporting strong leadership, safeguarding standards, and inclusive education, governors ensure every pupil has the opportunity to thrive. Governance is about doing the right thing for our pupils, every single time. At OHCAT, our governors are united by a shared purpose: to support, challenge, and lead with integrity. Their work ensures that every school in our Trust is a place where children thrive, staff are empowered, and communities are proud.” Raymond Leclercq, Chair of Trustees
For further information regarding the local governing body or for governance information please e-mail governance@ohcat.org
Governors demonstrate a strong drive for improvement and are keen that the school constantly evolves and adapts…They are well placed to hold leaders to account because they have a wealth of experience…Not only do they provide challenge for leaders, but they also hold one another to account.
The LGB generally meets once a term and comprises of people from the community with relevant skills and experience, parent and staff governors.
Additionally, the LGB has established a Pay Committee comprised of the Chair of the LGB and two further governors – these will be the HR portfolio holder and the Finance portfolio holder unless circumstances do not permit. The Pay Committee meets once a year to consider the Headteacher’s salary recommendations for all teaching staff, and to ensure that all pay decisions have been made in line with OHC&AT’s Pay Policy and OHC&AT’s Appraisal Policy.
